findings.evidence: the "invite-sent" section defines 0 controls whose target names another defined state (1 incoming link from elsewhere in the artifact).
findings.fix: Add a control inside the "invite-sent" section whose target is another state the artifact defines, for example a back, cancel, or continue control.
findings.violation: This state offers no control whose target names another state the artifact defines, so a user who reaches it has no path to leave it within the artifact.

findings.evidence: archive-confirm's copy states "You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list," and project-archived repeats "It no longer appears in the active projects list for anyone on the team," but no state or section named an archived-projects list exists anywhere in the artifact, and project-archived's only control is "Back to your projects," which targets workspace-overview, not an archive list.
findings.fix: Either add an archived-projects-list state reachable from workspace-overview with a restore control per project, or, if that is out of scope for this spec, remove the reversibility claim from the archive-confirm and project-archived copy.
findings.violation: Archiving is presented as reversible ("restore it at any time") but the artifact defines no restore control and no archived-projects-list state anywhere, so the reversal path the copy promises does not exist in the design as specified.

findings.evidence: project-settings-save-btn, invite-member-save-btn, and notification-settings-save-btn are all type="submit" buttons inside forms with no action or method attributes, and none of the three sections defines what the user sees while the save runs or once it finishes: no confirmation message, no changed control state, no transition to another defined state.
findings.fix: For each of the three Save buttons, specify what the user sees immediately after saving: a confirmation message, a visibly updated control, or a defined next state.
findings.location: the "project-settings", "invite-member", and "notification-settings" sections, their Save submit buttons
findings.violation: Three separate save actions in the artifact specify a trigger but no in-progress or result feedback, so a user who clicks Save on any of these three forms has no way to tell whether the change was applied.

findings.evidence: In project-settings and notification-settings, the form's "Save" button is the only commit-like control on the screen. In invite-member, "Save" is a type="submit" button inside the form, but a separate "Continue" link outside the form is what actually leads to "invite-sent" (the screen that reports the invite as sent), and the artifact does not say what, if anything, the "Save" button in invite-member commits.
findings.fix: Either remove the separate "Save" button from invite-member and have the form's own submit lead to invite-sent, or rename the two controls so their distinct effects are clear, e.g. "Save draft" and "Send invite."
findings.location: the "invite-member" section's "invite-member-save-btn" button, compared with "project-settings-save-btn" and "notification-settings-save-btn"
findings.violation: The label "Save" means "this commits the entered data, and that is the end of the interaction" in two of the three forms it appears in, but in invite-member a further "Continue" step is needed to reach the state where the invite is reported sent, so the same label does not stand for the same thing everywhere it appears.

findings.evidence: <button> with no text content and no accessible-name attribute
findings.fix: Add visible text to this control, or an aria-label attribute naming what it does.
findings.violation: This control has neither visible text nor an accessible-name attribute, so nothing on screen names what the control does.

findings.evidence: workspace-overview-promo-referral reads "Invite 3 teammates this month to unlock the advanced reporting add-on," but invite-member offers a single email field and a single Continue action per visit, with no way to enter more than one address or invite in bulk.
findings.fix: Add a way to invite more than one teammate per visit to invite-member, such as a repeatable email field, a comma-separated list, or an "invite another" action that stays on the same screen.
findings.location: the "workspace-overview" section's promo text, and the "invite-member" section
findings.violation: The artifact's own copy treats inviting 3 teammates as the task at hand, but the only invite path defined requires navigating into invite-member, entering one address, continuing, and returning, three separate times, with no bulk or multi-address route offered.

findings.evidence: workspace-overview-promo-referral ("Invite 3 teammates this month to unlock the advanced reporting add-on") sits between the recent-projects list and both primary navigation links ("Open project settings", "View last import result") in reading order.
findings.fix: Move the promotional banner below the primary navigation links, or elsewhere off this screen, so the two links a user comes to this screen for are not preceded by unrelated promotional content.
findings.violation: This screen's task is seeing your projects and navigating to project settings or the last import result; the promotional add-on banner is not part of either task, yet it is placed ahead of both primary links in reading order, pushing them down.
